3. Passive thermal bound and finite heat-transfer calculation.

Consider an unpowered device with positive passive thermal paths, positive heat capacities and latent enthalpy, initial temperatures at most70C, ambient no hotter than70C and a real contacting tool whose actual boundary never exceeds70C. No interior source or other hotter stock is supplied. At any device node first reaching70C, every conductive/radiative exchange with its neighbours is nonpositive into that node. Therefore the node cannot cross that boundary. A phase-change plateau adds positive stored enthalpy but does not create heat. This is a conditional maximum-principle argument for a passive thermal network, not a physical tool or an all-fault guarantee.

The executable example includes joint and neighbour heat capacities4e-5J/K each,25C ambient conductance2e-4W/K each, four declared metal-like bridges with flux n*L/(2R)*(Tj_K^2-Tn_K^2), L2.44e-8, melting60C and latent enthalpy2mJ. These are INTRODUCED, not a fit to Indalloy19. A finite shared head has C=.05J/K, ambient conductance.0005W/K, maximum heater.1W and continuous introduced feedback targeting70C. At the70C head boundary, the feedback heat equals its ambient loss and any outward contact heat makes the derivative nonpositive. That establishes the head cap inside this mathematical controller model, not with a free real sensor or fault detector.

Cold head preparation takes25.4892s and2.54892J in the declared warmup model. Holding the ready head at70C consumes22.5mW; cold start and standby remain paid. Eight-second intervals report heater energy separately from cold start; these are not complete rework service costs.

At contact conductance.002W/K and R.01ohm/bridge, the model reaches95% melt at.4075s. An INTRODUCED.25s later it opens the conductor paths and detaches the thermal head; the joint/neighbor peak62.5214/60.3552C, and both return below30C at1.3463s. At R.1ohm the corresponding release is.3111s and neighbour peak48.5999C. Conductance.001W/K reaches only57.3248C at R.01 and58.9243C at R.1 within8s: a safe temperature cap does not supply enough heat transfer to melt. Conductance.005W/K gives.0880s release and64.2413C neighbour peak at R.01. Every case remains below70C in the declared model.
